text:
Marisol (Docs): build failed on publish: linkcheck flagged anchors with backticks and parentheses. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4899. Error excerpt:

```
WARN Broken link: /docs/reference/sdk#\`Client.get_version()\` -> target not in HTML
at validateAnchors (linkcheck.py:142)
```

Ethan (Eng): That page was migrated from MkDocs -> Docusaurus last week. MkDocs slugified `Client.get_version()` differently (it removed periods), Docusaurus keeps parens in some slugifier versions. Mixed slugs cause these failures.

Sam (DevEx): Quick repro: create heading `## Client.get_version()` and run node slug library used by the site: `npx slugify-heading "Client.get_version()"` -> output differs by version. We should avoid relying on default slugs for code-containing headings.

Marisol (Docs): The offending heading is `## \`Client.get_version()\` helper` (backticks + parens). People like code snippets in headings though..

Priya (Eng): Fast unblock: I added explicit ids to three pages in PR #4902, e.g., `## \`Client.get_version()\` helper {#client-get-version}` and updated cross-links to use the id. That fixed the immediate broken anchor failures in CI.

InfraBot: CI job docs/linkcheck (build 4899) finished 7 broken anchors remaining7. See https://ci.redwood-inference.com/jobs/4899

Sam (DevEx): For a durable fix we should: 1) add a Rehype plugin to normalize slugs across build and linkcheck (custom slugify that strips punctuation, collapses runs of non-alphanum to hyphens), 2) add a docs lint rule warning on headings that contain inline code or parentheses recommending explicit ids, 3) add a migration script to backfill ids on migrated MkDocs pages where slugs previously matched links.

Ethan (Eng): Happy to own the Rehype plugin PR. I'll prototype a slugify that matches the old MkDocs behavior (lowercase, remove punctuation, replace dots and parens with hyphens). I'll run it in a branch and run full linkcheck.

Marisol (Docs): Also adding a tiny CONTRIBUTING paragraph: "Avoid placing raw inline code or trailing punctuation in headings. Use explicit heading ids when linking from other pages." Keeps writers aware.

Priya (Eng): FYI I opened a small follow-up to change a few long internal links to use relative id links rather than page+anchor when the target is in the same docs nav. Less fragile. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4905

Sam (DevEx): I'll add the grep-lint first as advisory so we don't block old content, and then we can flip to error after a 2-week grace period.

Marisol (Docs): Merged the three-id patch and the minor links update. Re-run CI: linkcheck is green for those items. Remaining failures are from old external redirects (filing tickets). Thanks all! :sparkles:

Ethan (Eng): Follow-up task list in the infra board: add rehype-slug plugin, backfill ids migration script, update linkcheck to use canonical slug logic. Assigning to me + Sam.

Marisol (Docs): Closing thread, moving to #docs-ops board cards.
